text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The European Commission forecast an Italian deficit/GDP ratio of 3.2 percent this year, missing the 3,0 percent EMU target, and said the deficit next year was set to swell to 3.9 percent of GDP. But the report said Italy's 1997 ratio could meet the single currency test of 3.0 percent if existing and new measures proved effective (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi slammed the European Commission for its forecast, saying it had not taken account of all available data and calling it "incomprehensive", considering the recent economic efforts made by the country in order to meet the goal. He also said he would not resign (all).

* In an interview, opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said Prodi's majority coalition had failed its commitment to make sure the country would join the first EMU group and Italy would never qualify for Europe's single currency as long as hard left Communist Refoundation was an ally of the government. Berlusconi's proposal also included a two year coalition between majority and opposition before calling new elections (La Repubblica).
* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed Italian industrial orders fell 3.7 year-on-year in January, while turnover fell 3.9 percent (Sole 24 Ore).
* Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino said Belgium's Kredietbank would take a two percent stake in the the group to form part of the Italian bank's core of stable shareholders (all).
* A report by the research office of Italy's employers' association Confindustria showed Italian industrial output rose 0.7 percent in March and April 1997 compared with January and February (all).

* Austrian postal and telecoms monopoly PTA said Italy's telecoms holding STET had offered 8.4 billion schillings for a 25 percent stake in Mobilkom Austria, the country's biggest mobile phone network. The deal is due to be subject to regulatory clearance by the European Commission. STET also forecast that mobile phones would account for one quarter of Austrian market by 2000 (all).

* The latest monthly survey by economic research institute ISCO showed confidence in the economy among Italian households fell to 108.1 in April from 108.6 in March and against 108.8 in April 1995 (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
